tasks.title: One SQLite fixture base for the seven Infrastructure persistence test classes: Migrate instead of EnsureCreated, sealed leaves over a Dispose(bool) base, and the AreaPersistence rename (MASTER-014, MASTER-065, MASTER-127, MASTER-042)
acceptance: `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/Persistence/SqliteInMemoryTestBase.cs` exists, declares `public abstract class SqliteInMemoryTestBase : IDisposable` in namespace `DungeonMaster.Tests.Infrastructure.Persistence`, and carries EXACTLY the six members frozen in contracts/sqlite-fixture-base.md section 3 -- `protected DbContextOptions<AppDbContext> Options { get; }`, `protected AppDbContext CreateContext()`, `protected IDbContextFactory<AppDbContext> CreateDbContextFactory()`, `protected IUnitOfWorkFactory CreateFactory()`, `public void Dispose()`, `protected virtual void Dispose(bool disposing)`. Any additional member is a contract change and needs an escalation, not a decision. The declaration lines are quoted. It is a NEW type: promoting one of the seven existing classes is prohibited by the user's re-scope decision, because sealing it afterwards would contradict MASTER-127.

MASTER-127: the disposal shape is exactly contracts/sqlite-fixture-base.md section 4 -- `Dispose()` NOT virtual, calling `Dispose(true)` then `GC.SuppressFinalize(this)`; `Dispose(bool)` virtual. All seven leaves are `public sealed class <X> : SqliteInMemoryTestBase` and none declares `Dispose`. Evidence: `grep -rn "class .*: *IDisposable\|class .*, *IDisposable" --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Tests | grep -v sealed | wc -l` returns 1 (the base); the same command returned 7 at 850a10b. BOTH numbers are quoted with the command, and the pre-task 7 is re-measured on the base commit rather than inherited.

MASTER-014: the base applies the schema with `Database.Migrate()`, and `grep -rn "EnsureCreated" --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Tests | grep -v '/bin/\|/obj/'` returns NOTHING. The same command returned 7 call sites in 7 distinct classes at 850a10b -- re-measure that on the base commit and quote both results. Three of the seven (`UnitOfWorkTests`, `AreaOutlineChangeTrackingTests`, `PlacedObjectConfigurationTests`) appear in neither TEST-002's nor TEST-009's `locations` list, and two of those three live under `Configurations/` rather than `Repositories/`; the audit under-counts and a fix scoped to four files has not done this task.

MASTER-014 gets a ratchet, not a side effect. A new named `[Fact]` in `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/Persistence/SqliteInMemoryTestBaseTests.cs` asserts BOTH that `GetPendingMigrations()` is empty AND that `GetAppliedMigrations().Count()` equals the number of migration files on disk. That number is re-derived by the task with `ls src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Migrations/*.cs | grep -v Designer | grep -v Snapshot | wc -l` (it returned 3 at 850a10b: InitialCreate, AddFloorDescription, UtcDateTimeTimestampsAndScaleWithoutStoreDefault) and quoted with that command. A CARDINALITY assertion is required and a non-emptiness assertion is NOT sufficient: an assertion that some migration was applied stays green when a migration is added and never applied, which is the exact hole MASTER-014 exists to close.

That new fact is shown able to fail by injection with a passing control. Injection: add a fourth, empty migration to the Infrastructure project without changing what the fixture applies, observe the count assertion FAIL, then remove it and observe the fact PASS again (the positive control). The command and both observed outcomes are quoted. `Verified by inspection` does not satisfy this. If the injection cannot be made to compile or to fail, say so and report the criterion NOT met rather than reporting it met -- a prescribed injection that leaves its named test green certifies nothing.

The two residual risks the spike named are checked and reported rather than discovered later. (a) No test reads columns positionally: `grep -rn "SELECT \*\|GetOrdinal\|GetValue(0)" --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Tests | grep -v '/bin/\|/obj/'` and its result are quoted. (b) No test enumerates `sqlite_master`: `grep -rni "sqlite_master" --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Tests | grep -v '/bin/\|/obj/'` and its result are quoted. `Migrate()` adds `__EFMigrationsHistory` and `__EFMigrationsLock`, which `EnsureCreated()` did not; the report states that and names any test that could observe them. Both greps use bare member names, never a `Type.Member` form, because this codebase splits calls across lines and a qualified single-line grep misses a split call.

`TestDbContextFactory.cs` is not modified and all of its use sites still compile. Re-measure with `grep -rn "TestDbContextFactory" --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Tests | grep -v '/bin/\|/obj/' | grep -v "Repositories/TestDbContextFactory.cs:" | wc -l` and with the `-rl` form; at 850a10b these returned 10 use sites across 7 files. DISCREPANCY TO CARRY: spike-findings.md says 6 files. The architect re-measured 7 with the `-rl` form quoted above and used 7. The task re-measures again and reports its own figure. `git diff --stat` shows `TestDbContextFactory.cs` unchanged, quoted.

MASTER-065: the duplicated block exists once. `grep -rn "new SqliteConnection" --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Tests | grep -v '/bin/\|/obj/' | wc -l` returns 1, where it returned 7 at 850a10b -- re-measure both and quote them. No leaf declares `_connection`, `_options`, a constructor building either, `Dispose`, `CreateContext` or `CreateFactory`. The base provides `CreateContext()` and `CreateFactory()` UNCONDITIONALLY: measured across the seven classes, 5 of 7 declared `CreateContext` and 6 of 7 declared `CreateFactory`, so a base offering only the intersection breaks leaves and a base offering only what each leaf had is not a base.

MASTER-042 is ONE deletion. `RemoveArea_PersistsAcrossReload` is deleted -- it is line-for-line identical to `RemoveArea_WithEmptyOutline_PersistsAcrossReload` except that the wider test adds an outline assertion, so deleting the narrow one loses nothing. `UpdateArea_RenamePersistsAcrossReload` is RETAINED. The audit's prose points the wrong way and a criterion saying `drop the two subsumed tests` destroys real coverage: `UpdateArea_SecondRenamePersistsAcrossReload` reloads from the database and overwrites the name in a second unit of work, so the first rename's persistence is never observed. This was demonstrated by injection with a passing control -- removing the first `CommitAsync` leaves SecondRename green and makes RenamePersists fail. The task RE-RUNS that injection inside the new base-class shape and quotes the command and both observed outcomes, because the extraction changed the fixture the demonstration ran against.

MASTER-042 rename: the file becomes `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/AreaPersistenceTests.cs` and the class becomes `AreaPersistenceTests`. The XML summary is rewritten as a statement of what is GUARANTEED -- that this class holds the only persistence round-trip coverage of area removal and area rename, every other RemoveArea/UpdateArea hit being either an in-memory Domain aggregate test or a handler test against a substituted repository, and `AreaOutlineChangeTrackingTests` covering the different method `UpdateAreaOutline` -- and no longer describes an investigation. `git ls-files` returns nothing for the old path after the change; both the old and new paths are quoted.

Test-count reconciliation. The pre-task baseline passing count is RE-MEASURED with `dotnet test C:\dm-wt\6b-ii\src\DungeonMaster.Tests\DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj` and quoted with that command. The figure 695 is inherited from Spike A and is NOT adopted; where the re-measured figure differs, the re-measured figure is used and the discrepancy is reported. The post-task count is stated with the same command, and the difference is shown to be exactly -1 (the single MASTER-042 deletion) PLUS the tests added by the new `SqliteInMemoryTestBaseTests` class, each figure stated separately with its own command. No aggregate figure stands in for the arithmetic. If the delta is anything else, the task investigates before reporting done -- an unexplained delta means a leaf silently stopped being discovered, which is the exact risk of turning seven concrete classes into seven leaves.

Every count quoted from a run of the full test project is accompanied by `git status --porcelain`, and that output names ONLY files inside this task's ownership globs. A peer task in this worktree may hold a temporary source injection while you run, so an unexplained modified file makes any full-suite figure contaminated and unusable. Evidence for an INJECTION is taken from a `dotnet test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~<this task's own class>"` run and never from a full-suite run, so a peer's injection in another class cannot be mistaken for yours. If the clean-status condition cannot be met, the task reports that rather than quoting a number.
`dotnet build C:\dm-wt\6b-ii\src\DungeonMaster.sln` prints `Build succeeded. 0 Warning(s) 0 Error(s)`, quoted.

Every file this task creates or edits is tab-indented and CRLF. Verified per file by comparing `tr -cd '\r' | wc -c` against `tr -cd '\n' | wc -c` and quoting the equal pair. Conversion happens IMMEDIATELY after writing each file, before any build -- a `.cs` file left in LF state produces `0 Warning(s) / 176 Error(s)`, all IDE0055, under TreatWarningsAsErrors, and breaks concurrent peers. Neither `grep -c '^\t'` nor `grep -cv $'\r$'` appears anywhere in the evidence: `grep -cE "^\t..."` returns 0 on a fully tab-indented file because GNU ERE reads `\t` as a literal `t`, and the CR form varies by shell. This has recurred inside frozen criteria twice.

tasks.title: Extract the dungeon-missing not-found test into one base across twelve command handler test classes, add and DEMONSTRATE the commit-boundary assertion, and make internal interfaces substitutable (MASTER-085 command half plus the two re-scope additions)
acceptance: `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Handlers/DungeonNotFoundHandlerTestBase.cs` exists and follows contracts/shared-test-base-convention.md sections 2 and 3: `public abstract`, leaves `public sealed`, variation supplied by an abstract member the leaf overrides and NEVER by a constructor parameter, a `[MemberData]` table keyed on a type name, or reflection over the leaf. The base name ends `TestBase`, and its inherited fact names read correctly on all twelve leaves.

The base projects the result through an abstract member rather than constraining a type parameter. `Result` and `Result<T>` are two UNRELATED `public sealed record` types with no common base and no shared interface -- verified with `grep -n "sealed record Result" src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/Result.cs src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Results/ResultOfT.cs`, whose output is quoted -- so a generic base cannot read `IsSuccess` or `ErrorCategory` off `TResult`. The shape is an abstract member such as `protected abstract Task<(bool IsSuccess, ErrorCategory? ErrorCategory)> InvokeWithMissingDungeonAsync();`. No `dynamic`, no reflection, and no type constraint that does not exist. This fact was measured by the architect and is not in spike-findings.md; if it is wrong, report it with the command that shows otherwise.

The FOURTEEN command handler test classes share one constructor base, which is a SEPARATE requirement from the twelve-class not-found base and is not satisfied by it. Definition of done item 5 is checked by `the duplicated constructor body appearing in one file`, and at 850a10b it appears in fourteen: each class declares `_unitOfWork = new UnitOfWorkSubstitute();`, `_writeRepository = _unitOfWork.Dungeons;` and `_handler = new <X>Handler(_unitOfWork.Factory);`. `UnitOfWorkSubstitute` already consolidates the WIRING but not the per-class constructor. The shape is two levels: `CommandHandlerTestBase<THandler>` carrying the substitute and a `protected abstract THandler CreateHandler(IUnitOfWorkFactory factory);` that all 14 override, and `DungeonNotFoundHandlerTestBase` DERIVING from it for the 12 that arrange a missing dungeon. Both follow contracts/shared-test-base-convention.md sections 2 and 3, and both are above the section 1 threshold of three. Evidence: `grep -c "new UnitOfWorkSubstitute()" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Commands/*.cs` returns 14 non-zero files at 850a10b and 0 after (the construction having moved into the base), and `grep -ln ": CommandHandlerTestBase" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Commands/*.cs | wc -l` returns 14. Both commands and both before/after figures are quoted. NOTE for the reviewer: this criterion was added by the architect after Gate 2's amendments, on discovering that the manifest as drafted covered only the 12-class not-found half of definition-of-done item 5 and left the 14-class constructor half uncovered.

Exactly the twelve command classes that arrange a missing dungeon inherit the base. Re-measure the set with `grep -ln 'Returns((Dungeon?)null)' src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Commands/*.cs` (it listed 12 files at 850a10b) and show that the post-task count of `grep -ln ": DungeonNotFoundHandlerTestBase"` over the same directory EQUALS it. Both commands and both figures are quoted.

The two exclusions are stated correctly, against the audit. TEST-008 names CreateDungeon and DeleteDungeon as the two classes with no not-found test and it is WRONG about DeleteDungeon: `grep -n "NotFound" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Commands/DeleteDungeonCommandHandlerTests.cs` returns `65: HandleAsync_WithUnknownId_ReturnsNotFound` and `85: ErrorCategory.NotFound`, reached through `RemoveAsync(...).Returns(false)` rather than a null load. CreateDungeon is the only command class with no `NotFound` assertion at all. Neither inherits the base -- DeleteDungeon signals differently and additionally asserts that the error contains the id and that `CommitAsync` did not happen. The report quotes the command and states both exclusions with their reasons.

No assertion is lost. Per contracts/shared-test-base-convention.md section 4, the report quotes `git diff` for each of the twelve classes and names every assertion the pre-task dungeon-missing test made beyond `IsSuccess` and `ErrorCategory`, showing where each one survives -- in the leaf, or through an additional abstract hook. Silently dropping a per-class assertion is the failure mode this extraction is most likely to produce, and a green suite does not detect it.

The commit-boundary assertion is added ALONGSIDE, never in place of, the existing repository-boundary assertion. Measured at 850a10b in `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Commands/`: `grep -n "DidNotReceive" *.cs | wc -l` returns 13 sites across 10 files, of which 12 assert `.Update(Arg.Any<Dungeon>())` and 1 asserts `.CommitAsync(Arg.Any<CancellationToken>())` (`DeleteDungeonCommandHandlerTests.cs:89-90`); `grep -c "CommitAsync" *.cs | grep -v ':0'` shows the member in only 2 of the 14 files. Re-measure all three and quote them; NOTE that spike-findings.md cites only the four sites TEST-010 named, which under-states the fleet. Post-task each of those 12 tests ALSO asserts `_unitOfWork.UnitOfWork.DidNotReceive().CommitAsync(Arg.Any<CancellationToken>())`, every pre-existing `.Update(...)` assertion survives, and the base carries the same pair for the twelve not-found tests.

The claim that the commit boundary is strictly more observable is DEMONSTRATED, not asserted. spike-findings.md flags it as reasoning from read evidence, NOT measurement, and this task may not rely on it before showing it. Injection: in `src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Handlers/DungeonMutationExtensions.cs`, move `await unitOfWork.CommitAsync(ct);` to immediately AFTER the `LoadAsync` assignment in BOTH `MutateAsync` overloads, leaving every other line in place. This compiles -- nothing becomes unreachable, so CS0162 under TreatWarningsAsErrors does not fire, and `if (true) { return ...; }` would not compile here. Three observations, each quoted with the FILTERED command that produced it: (a) the new `CommitAsync` assertions FAIL; (b) the pre-existing `.Update(...)` assertions stay GREEN -- this is the discrimination and it is the whole claim; (c) POSITIVE CONTROL: with the file restored the same filtered run is fully green. If (b) does not hold, the claim is NOT established: report that and do NOT assert the commit boundary is more observable.

tasks.title: Make the two query-handler tests able to fail: element identity and cardinality, demonstrated by three run injections (MASTER-069), and settle MASTER-085's query equivalence class
acceptance: `GetDungeonDetailQueryHandlerTests.HandleAsync_WithExistingId_ReturnsDtoFromRepository` asserts `result.Should().BeSameAs(dto)`. `DungeonDetailDto` is a `public record` and therefore a reference type -- `grep -n "record DungeonDetailDto" src/DungeonMaster.Application/Features/Dungeons/Queries/GetDungeonDetail/DungeonDetailDto.cs`, quoted -- so `BeSameAs` compiles.

`GetDungeonsQueryHandlerTests.HandleAsync_WithDungeons_ReturnsSummaries` asserts cardinality AND per-ELEMENT identity: `result.Should().HaveCount(summaries.Count)` and each `result[i].Should().BeSameAs(summaries[i])`. Element identity is required; LIST identity is not, because a handler may legitimately materialise the sequence and `result.Should().BeSameAs(summaries)` would be a false constraint. DISCREPANCY TO CARRY, raised by the architect: spike-findings.md treats identity as closing only `the smaller half`, but for a reference type identity IMPLIES field equality, so the two halves separate only for the LIST, where the list object and its elements are different references. This criterion is written to close both halves regardless of which reading is right, and the injections below settle it empirically rather than by argument.

Three injections, each into the query handler under test, each RUN and not merely prescribed, each quoted with its command and its observed failure. (M1) IDENTITY: the handler returns a reconstructed value -- `dto with { }` for the detail handler, `.Select(s => s with { }).ToList()` for the summaries handler. (M2) AN UNNAMED FIELD: corrupt a field the PRE-task assertions never named -- for example `LastModified`, `FloorCount` or `Notes` -- via a `with` expression. (M3) ORDER OR CARDINALITY: `.Reverse().ToList()` or `.Take(1).ToList()` on the summaries. Each injection must compile; `if (true) { return ...; }` will not, because CS0162 is an error here. For EACH of the three the report ALSO states whether it would have failed the PRE-task test -- that figure measures the size of the hole this task closes, and spike-findings.md measured only one of three caught before.

POSITIVE CONTROL: with every injection reverted, a `dotnet test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~QueryHandlerTests"` run is fully green, quoted. An experiment in which everything fails cannot distinguish detection from a broken apparatus, and this control is what makes the three failures above evidence.

`src/DungeonMaster.Application/Features/Dungeons/Queries/**` ends BYTE-IDENTICAL to its state at 850a10b. Those files are in this task's `owns` ONLY to license the injections above; no permanent change to Application source is in scope. Evidence: pre-injection byte copies in this task's scratch directory, and after restoration BOTH `git status --porcelain src/DungeonMaster.Application` (empty) and an `md5sum` comparison per file, quoted.

MASTER-085's second equivalence class is a SETTLED DECISION, taken by the user at Gate 2, and NOT an unfinished extraction. The two query test classes KEEP their own constructors and no base type is introduced under `Queries/`. contracts/shared-test-base-convention.md section 1 sets the extraction threshold at three or more classes sharing the shape; the query classes number two. The report states BOTH the rule and the measured count -- re-measure with `ls src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Queries/*.cs | wc -l` and quote the command with its result -- and states in terms that the decision was taken and the count is why. A reviewer finding two unextracted query classes is looking at the intended end state: this criterion is met by the absence of a base, recorded with its count, and a report that omits the count leaves the decision indistinguishable from an omission and does NOT meet it. The threshold of 3 stands unamended; if the implementer believes two warrants a base, that is an ESCALATION to the orchestrator and never a unilateral extraction.

tasks.title: Collapse the four name-only validator test classes onto one generic abstract base, with per-leaf discrimination demonstrated by injection (MASTER-064)
acceptance: A generic abstract base -- named per contracts/shared-test-base-convention.md section 3, for example `NameOnlyValidatorTestBase<TCommand>` -- exists under `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Validators/`, is `public abstract`, and takes its variation from an abstract member the leaf overrides (a factory such as `protected abstract TCommand CreateCommandWithName(string? name);`), never from a constructor parameter and never from reflection over the leaf.

EXACTLY four classes inherit it: `AddAreaCommandValidatorTests`, `CreateDungeonCommandValidatorTests`, `UpdateAreaCommandValidatorTests`, `UpdateDungeonCommandValidatorTests`. Each is `public sealed` and keeps its own file name. Evidence: `wc -l` over all 14 `*ValidatorTests.cs` files, quoted, showing those four at 55 lines at 850a10b and every other file at a different length. The four differ from one another on exactly three constructions plus their using, class name and validator field -- `diff` between any two of them is quoted for one pair.

Scope does not grow, and the reason is measured. `AddFloorCommandValidatorTests` and `UpdateFloorCommandValidatorTests` do NOT inherit: their validators carry `MaximumLength(100)` WITHOUT `NotEmpty()`, plus separate `NotEmpty()` rules on `DungeonId`/`FloorId`, and their files are 76 and 108 lines rather than 55. Six validators mention `MaximumLength(100)` but only four have the sole rule `RuleFor(c => c.Name).NotEmpty().MaximumLength(100)`. Re-measure with `grep -rn "MaximumLength(100)" --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Application | grep -v '/obj/'` and quote it; use the bare member name and never a `Type.Member` form, because a qualified single-line grep misses a call split across lines and this codebase splits many.

The OTHER TEN validator test classes are untouched, which definition-of-done item 6 names explicitly. Evidence: `git diff --stat src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Validators/` is quoted and names ONLY the four leaves, the new base file, and -- if and only if it needed no change, in which case it should not appear at all -- nothing else. Any of the other ten appearing in that output is a blocking finding: MASTER-064's scope is four classes, the measurement showing why is in this task's scope criterion, and a diff that touches an eleventh file has grown the entry rather than closed it.

The three tests are preserved exactly as BEHAVIOUR: valid command passes; a three-case `[Theory]` on `""`, `"   "` and `null` asserting `IsValid` false and a single error on the `Name` property; and a 101-character name asserting the same. The property assertion must still resolve through `nameof` on the LEAF's command type. A base that asserts on the literal string `"Name"` has replaced a compile-checked reference with an uncheckable one and is a BLOCKING finding, not a stylistic one.

tasks.title: Correct the seven measured mis-citations in docs/audit/05-tests.md in place, each carrying its command, its anchor commit, and a measurement-error-versus-drift classification
acceptance: Every command this task runs to verify a figure is anchored to a FIXED COMMIT and never to the working tree: `git grep -n <pattern> 850a10b -- <path>`, `git show 850a10b:<path>`, or `git show 2603170:<path>` piped to the counting command. This is load-bearing twice over. T1 through T5 may be running concurrently in this worktree and are changing the very code these figures count, so a working-tree command returns a different number depending on when it runs; and a reviewer must be able to re-run each command MONTHS later and get the number the correction states. A figure verified against the working tree does not satisfy any criterion in this task.

Each of the seven corrections is CLASSIFIED, and the classification is itself measured rather than assumed. Two classes: MEASUREMENT ERROR -- the entry was wrong on the day it was written -- and DRIFT -- the entry was accurate on 2026-08-17 and the repository moved underneath it. The audit was authored at `2603170` (`git log --diff-filter=A -- docs/audit/05-tests.md`, re-run and quoted), so the test is whether the claim held AT `2603170`. Determine it with evidence, per item: for a file-count claim, `git log --diff-filter=A -- <file>` on each file the entry misses, to establish whether the file existed then; for a deleted-code claim, the deleting commit's date; for a reasoning claim, the state of the cited code at `2603170`. Do NOT guess a classification and do NOT default to DRIFT because it is the kinder reading -- an entry excused as drift when it was a counting error teaches the next reader to trust the wrong thing. Where the evidence does not settle it, the amendment says UNDETERMINED and says why.

Every correction is made IN PLACE and carries an amendment block in the form this repository already uses. The precedent is `.dir-sdlc/sessions/2026-09-02-app-sub-suite-rebuild/contracts/anti-vacuity.md` section 1.1, which corrects its own inventory with a `**[AMENDED E8, 2026-09-02. ...]**` block; read it before writing the first one and follow its shape. Each block states, at minimum: the PREVIOUS WORDING VERBATIM, so the original claim survives and is not overwritten; the measured figure that replaces it; the exact command that produced that figure, anchored per the anchoring criterion; the commit the measurement is anchored to; and the MEASUREMENT ERROR / DRIFT / UNDETERMINED classification with its own evidence. A correction that silently swaps a number for another number does not satisfy this criterion however right the new number is: a reader in six months must be able to tell a counting mistake from ordinary repository movement, and that distinction is the entire reason this task exists rather than a find-and-replace.

CORRECTION 1 -- the seven-versus-four count, in TWO entries. `TEST-002`'s body says `All four Infrastructure test classes create their schema with` and its `locations` list has 4 entries; `TEST-009`'s TITLE says `copy-pasted verbatim into four Infrastructure test classes` and its body says `the same nineteen lines exist four times`, with 4 `locations`. The measured figure is SEVEN, in seven distinct classes: `git grep -n "EnsureCreated" 850a10b -- src/DungeonMaster.Tests` (re-run and quoted). Three of the seven appear in NEITHER entry's list -- `UnitOfWorkTests.cs`, `Configurations/AreaOutlineChangeTrackingTests.cs`, `Configurations/PlacedObjectConfigurationTests.cs` -- and two of those three live under `Configurations/` rather than `Repositories/`, which is why a directory-scoped reading of either entry misses them. BOTH entries' titles, bodies and `locations` lists are corrected, and the three missing paths are added to both lists.

CORRECTION 2 -- the migration count. `TEST-002`'s body says `bypassing the two migrations under` `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Migrations/`. The measured figure is THREE -- `InitialCreate`, `AddFloorDescription`, `UtcDateTimeTimestampsAndScaleWithoutStoreDefault` -- from `git ls-tree -r --name-only 850a10b -- src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Migrations/ | grep '\.cs$' | grep -v Designer | grep -v Snapshot | wc -l`, re-run and quoted. The three names are listed in the amendment so the count is checkable rather than merely restated.

CORRECTION 3 -- the block length. `TEST-009`'s body says `the same nineteen lines exist four times`. The measured figure is SEVENTEEN lines, of which 13 are non-blank and non-doc, for the block running from `private readonly SqliteConnection` through `public void Dispose()`; it is byte-identical across all seven files modulo the constructor name (md5 `af38458e567a2e4f8b577f22e7437cfa`). Nineteen is reachable only by including `CreateContext()`, which is NOT present in all seven -- 5 of 7 declare `CreateContext`, 6 of 7 declare `CreateFactory`, 4 of 7 declare both. The amendment states 17, the 13 non-blank figure, the command that produced them, and the reason nineteen was reachable, because a bare number swap here would leave the next reader making the same mistake.

CORRECTION 4 -- `TEST-008`, two separate defects in one entry. (a) The constructor it DESCRIBES no longer exists: it says `Substitute.For<IDungeonWriteRepository>()` and `new XHandler(_writeRepository)`, whereas all 14 command classes use `UnitOfWorkSubstitute` and `new HANDLER(_unitOfWork.Factory)` -- `Application/Common/Handlers/UnitOfWorkSubstitute.cs`, `The one place the substituted unit-of-work chain is wired`, extracted by a prior session -- and its cited line ranges are stale to match. (b) Its stated exclusions are WRONG: it says CreateDungeon and DeleteDungeon are the two classes with no not-found test, but `git grep -n "NotFound" 850a10b -- src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Commands/DeleteDungeonCommandHandlerTests.cs` returns `65: HandleAsync_WithUnknownId_ReturnsNotFound` and `85: ErrorCategory.NotFound`, reached through `RemoveAsync(...).Returns(false)` rather than a null load. CreateDungeon is the ONLY command class with no `NotFound` assertion at all. Both defects are corrected and classified SEPARATELY -- (a) and (b) are not the same kind of error and must not share one amendment block.

CORRECTION 5 -- `TEST-013`, three defects. (a) `locations` entry 4, `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Map/SnapZoneCalculatorTests.cs:11-69`, refers to a file that does not exist: `SnapZoneCalculator` and its five facts were deleted in `1678d12`. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 850a10b | grep -i snapzone` returns nothing, quoted.
